messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Re: plot settings (axis name)
parts:
Hi Marcelo, try this: 

graf1 + theme(axis.title = element_text())

Does that work? I think you also may need ylab() instead of xlab() if you're using coord_flip(). 

Jonah

parts:
If you want, you can also preview the makeover coming to some of our plots by trying out the in-development bayesplot package here (will be moved to stan-dev soon). The version of the plot you're making would be this (using one of the Stan demo models as an example): 

devtools::install_github("jgabry/bayesplot") # temporary home

library("rstan")
library("bayesplot")

fit <- stan_demo("eight_schools")
x <- as.matrix(fit, pars = "theta")

mcmc_intervals(x)

mcmc_intervals(x) + 
    ylab("Parameters") +
    coord_flip() + 
    theme_default(x_lab = TRUE, y_lab = FALSE)

Changing the parameter labels will also be much easier, as you can just change any of the column names of the x matrix instead of having to mess with the ggplot object. 

Jonah

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: [stan-users] Re: plot settings (axis name)
parts:
The plots are just made using ggplot2 so what you can do after it's created is a question of what ggplot2 let's you do. The things you asked about all are set using theme elements, 

e.g. graph + theme(axis.line.x = element_line(size = 0.3))

Check out the ggplot2 documentation on theme elements (online doc better than in pkg) for more on that. 

bayesplot will make a lot of those things easier. If you open an issue here https://github.com/jgabry/bayesplot/issues
we'll help you get it installed. It's also still in development so if some features you want aren't currently available we're definitely looking for suggestions. 

Jonah
